newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares make third day of record highs.
newsitem.headline: German shares make third day of record highs.

text.p: German shares ended at record closing levels for the third day running on Thursday, boosted by gains in the banking sector and continuing a rally begun late on Tuesday when the dollar came off lows.

Dealers said the DAX index of 30 leading shares was still aiming for the technical and psychological level of 2,800 points and said it could reach that level on Friday, the last day of trading before shares in national telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom hit the market.
The blue-chip DAX index touched an all-time bourse high of 2,785.16 points in early dealings, then pared gains to end up 3.58 points at a record bourse close of 2,777.01 points.
In post-bourse IBIS electronic trading, the DAX ended at 2,784.39 points, up 13.78 points, or 0.50 percent, an IBIS closing high, just off the all-time high of 2,789.94 points reached in the morning.
Computer dealings were encouraged by a firmer dollar against the mark, German bond strength and a confident opening on Wall Street.

The day's main action was in the banking sector, with over four million Deutsche Bank AG shares and over four million Commerzbank AG shares changing hands in computer trade. Over a million Commerzbank shares were also traded in bourse dealings.

Thursday's best performer was Commerzbank which ended computer dealings up 1.4 marks, or almost four percent at 36.65 marks, having jumped over five percent in pre-bourse dealings on merger talk in the market.

But Commerzbank moved to quash merger speculation, saying it saw no one single large investor buying up the group's shares and said the strong rise in its share price was largely due to the fact that the shares were earlier undervalued.

The whole banking sector was buoyed by merger fever, Dresdner Bank rising over three percent or 1.38 marks to 44.58 points, while Deutsche Bank was up over two percent or 1.66 marks to 72.11 marks in electronic trade.
Outside of the banking sector, diversified industrial group Daimler Benz AG was also heavily traded and hit a year high of 99.70 marks in pre-bourse dealings.
But the stock could not penetrate the 100 mark level and later fell back on profit-taking to end down 1.35 marks at 97.75 marks.
Shares in national airline Lufthansa AG also fell, ending down 30 pfennigs at 20.25 marks after the German governmant said it would plan to sell the rest of its 36 percent stake in the firm.
